title: Astrid and the Crown
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish, bone-carver Cyrus Iversen discovers the wards were anchored to a living soul — Astrid, a runaway princess whose memories were carved away to hide her from the crown that wants her dead. Guided by the voices in his bones, Cyrus smuggles her through a country unraveling into old hatreds, pursued by her uncle's hunters and by the ghost-king who engineered the blackout. To restore the stars, Astrid must reclaim her memories — including the truth that she herself broke the wards to escape an arranged sacrifice. In the end she takes the crown not to rule but to dissolve it, paying with her own name, which only Cyrus remembers.
about_author: S. M. Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bone carvings before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about memory, grief, and the small mercies people trade for survival.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In his mountain workshop, Cyrus hears a new voice among the dead begging for passage, just as every star above Thornfell goes dark and the border wards shatter like glass. He packs his carving knives and flees into the chaos. Emotional beat: dread sharpened by a lifetime of keeping his gift secret.

chapters.title: A Girl Without a Name
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. On a smuggler's road he finds a young woman with no memories, clutching a broken wardstone that hums against his bones. The dead whisper that she is the anchor of the fallen wards. He lies to her about who she might be. Beat: reluctant compassion born of guilt.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Terrified and hollow, Astrid tests Cyrus's claim that he can hear the dead, pressing her hand to a carved relic and hearing her own voice speak a language she doesn't know. She realizes someone took her past deliberately. Beat: vertigo of self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Toll
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Royal hunters led by Captain Veyra reach the valley, posting sketches of a missing princess. Cyrus recognizes Astrid's face in the drawing and must decide whether to sell her out or run. Beat: the first true betrayal of his own safety.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A tense journey through flooded mine tunnels where the dead grow louder as the starless dark deepens; Astrid saves Cyrus's life using reflexes she can't explain. Beat: trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Ghost-King's Bargain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In a ruined shrine, the ghost of an ancient king offers Astrid her memories back piece by piece — for a price paid later. Cyrus warns her against it; she accepts one fragment anyway and sees a throne room soaked in blood. Beat: temptation and foreboding.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In a refugee city on the edge of panic, they seek an old fence who once knew Cyrus's mother. Instead they find Veyra waiting, and only a crowd rioting over the vanished stars lets them slip away. Beat: paranoia closing in.

chapters.title: Fragment: The Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The second memory fragment reveals she was to be sacrificed to renew the wards at midwinter — and that she chose to break them instead. She hides this from Cyrus. Beat: shame curdling into secrecy.

chapters.title: The Bone-Singer of Halvard
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. They seek a blind bone-singer who might restore Astrid's mind; she reads Cyrus's bones instead and tells him he is dying slowly from carrying too many voices. Beat: grief for a future he never let himself want.

chapters.title: Veyra's Truth
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The captain interrogates captured smugglers and uncovers that the king's brother ordered the princess's death, not rescue. Her loyalty cracks. Beat: disillusionment of a soldier.

chapters.title: Midwinter Crossing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A blizzard crossing where Astrid nearly dies and Cyrus confesses he has known who she is since the first night. She feels betrayed by his silence. Beat: the relationship fractures.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Court
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Captured and brought before Prince Aldric, Astrid plays the amnesiac while piecing together that he engineered both the sacrifice and the hunt. Veyra, guarding her cell, begins to doubt aloud. Beat: quiet, deadly cat-and-mouse.

chapters.title: Escape from Glasshall
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus trades his most precious carved relic to buy a way inside, then springs Astrid with Veyra's grudging help. The ghost-king's price comes due: he demands Astrid finish collecting her memories at the old capital. Beat: desperate momentum.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Carried
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid learns how much of himself Cyrus has lost to the dead over the years — names, songs, his mother's face — and understands his silence was fear, not deceit. Fragile reconciliation. Beat: tenderness after rupture.

chapters.title: The Road of Old Hatreds
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The countryside slides toward civil war as lords blame each other for the darkened sky; the trio witnesses a village massacre and Veyra openly breaks with the crown. Beat: the cost of survival made collective.

chapters.title: Fragment: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the capital's gates, the final memory arrives unbidden: Astrid's own mother helped design the sacrifice, believing it merciful. Astrid breaks down and nearly walks into Aldric's hands. Beat: despair at the bottom of the well.

chapters.title: The Hollow Crown
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the throne room beneath a starless sky, the ghost-king reveals he orchestrated everything to be crowned through Astrid's restored soul. Cyrus offers his remaining years of hearing in exchange for her freedom. Beat: sacrifice offered freely.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid claims the crown herself, flooding the wards with her whole remembered identity — including her guilt — and the stars return one by one. The ghost-king unravels; Aldric falls to his own hunters. Beat: triumphant, terrible climax.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The magic exacts its fee: Astrid's name and face fade from every living memory except Cyrus's, and even hers grows thin. Veyra holds the city together as regent of a crown that no longer rules. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: Carving a New Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid chooses a plain new life and a plain new name, asking Cyrus to carve her story into bone so someone, someday, will know. He refuses to forget her, whatever it costs him. Beat: quiet resolve.

chapters.title: The Last Voice
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus releases the accumulated dead he has carried, one voice at a time, until only Astrid's remains beside him — alive, unnamed, staying by choice. Beat: release and chosen companionship.

chapters.title: Stars Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. A year later, travelers cross open borders under ordinary stars, passing a roadside carver's stall where a woman sells small bone stars and a man listens to nothing at all. Beat: peace earned, memory kept in the smallest things.
